Amid all of US President Donald Trump's chronic self-contradictions, his self-
serving desire to shape the global economy is a rare constant. The oil crisis
stoked by Trump's war on Iran may have exposed the limits of such efforts, but
his public statements and social media posts on the war show he maintains his
aim to bend markets to his will.

Furthermore, as Trump sends prices dropping or soaring, anonymous traders seem
to be [turning](https://www.axios.com/2026/03/25/trump-iran-oil-insider-
trading) foreknowledge of executive actions into financial gain.

While the nation's wealthiest exploit stock and prediction markets, regulatory
bodies are increasingly uninterested in stopping financial crimes. The number
of enforcement cases [filed](https://www.newyorker.com/news/the-financial-
page/who-struck-it-rich-in-the-markets-when-trump-postponed-bombing-iran) by
the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is
[down](https://www.banking.senate.gov/newsroom/minority/warren-questions-sec-
chair-atkins-on-misleading-congress-about-record-low-agency-enforcement-
activity) 20% from those pursued by his predecessor under the Biden
administration. The Trump-appointed SEC chair, Paul Atkins, recently
[refused](https://www.facebook.com/SenLBR/videos/watch-trumps-sec-
commissioner-just-refused-to-say-insider-trading-is-bad/25982835198009882/) to
say that insider trading is always bad. Over at the Commodity Futures Trading
Commission, the enforcement agency for futures markets, the current head
[created](https://www.newyorker.com/news/the-financial-page/who-struck-it-
rich-in-the-markets-when-trump-postponed-bombing-iran) an "innovation task
force" for industries key to the Trump family. Ben Schiffrin, a former
attorney at the SEC, notes that Atkins is prioritizing the promotion of AI,
crypto, and prediction markets ahead of his regulatory responsibilities.

In these free-for-all conditions, **Zeteo** is breaking down seven instances
of suspicious trading resulting from the president's statements:

### **1. 'Liberation Day' Loopholes**

In March 2025, ahead of Trump's various tariff announcements, including the
sweeping "Liberation Day" statement that tanked the market, multiple executive
branch officials [made](https://www.propublica.org/article/us-officials-stock-
sales-trump-tariffs) "well-timed trades." As ProPublica reported, such traders
included a top US trade official and multiple longtime State Department
officials. A US ambassador, Gautam
[Rana](https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/news/426542/us-ambassador-to-leave-
slovakia-in-
january#:~:text=US%20Ambassador%20to%20Slovakia%20Gautam,the%20post%20since%20September%202022.),
sold between $830,000 and $1.7 million worth of stock in two weeks ahead of
Trump's announcement.

Tyler Gellasch, who runs the Healthy Markets Association, an ethics group,
told [ProPublica](https://www.propublica.org/article/us-officials-stock-sales-
trump-
tariffs#:~:text=To%20the%20extent%20they%20have,wild%20swings%20in%20the%20market.)
that such trading "undermines trust in government and the markets" and makes
"our markets look rigged."
